options.text: Clones from nuclear transfer have different cytoplasm from their parent

options.text: Clones carried in successive pregnancies have different uterine environments

notes.A: Mitochondrial DNA comes from the egg.

questions.stem: Which is the first layer that differentiates from the embryoblast?
questions.why: The hypoblast (primitive endoderm) is the first layer to appear from the inner cell mass, about day 8.

notes.A: It forms after the epiblast cavitates.
notes.D: The epiblast forms with it but the hypoblast is described first.

questions.stem: After implantation, which embryonic tissue is in direct contact with maternal tissue (endometrium)?
Which of the following arises directly from embryoblast?
questions.why: The inner cell mass splits into epiblast and hypoblast.

notes.C: From yolk sac or epiblast later.

questions.stem: At which stage of development does implantation occur?
questions.why: The blastocyst implants about day 6–7.

questions.stem: Which of the following events is decisive for initiation of implantation?
questions.why: The blastocyst must hatch from the zona before it can attach.

notes.C: Earlier, needed but not the trigger.

questions.stem: Which phase of development is the endometrium in at the commencement of implantation?
Which decidua in NOT in direct contact with any trophoblast throughout embryonic development?
questions.why: The decidua parietalis lines the rest of the uterus; it never touches trophoblast directly.

questions.stem: Splitting of the embryo can give identical twins at the:
questions.why: Splitting at 2-cell or morula gives separate chorions; at blastocyst (most common) one chorion.

questions.stem: Which is the commonest site of ectopic implantation?
Which are the first cells to differentiate from the morula?
questions.why: The morula separates into outer trophoblast and inner cell mass.

notes.C: From the inner cell mass, later.

questions.stem: The term for the changes the endometrium undergoes in response to implantation is:
What are the cells produced by cleavage of the zygote called?
Implantation at which site gives rise to placenta praevia?
questions.why: Implantation low in the uterus, near the internal os, gives placenta praevia.

questions.stem: Which of the following results from fusion of the male and female pronuclei?
The syncytiotrophoblast:

options.label: B
options.text: Gives rise to the decidua basalis

options.label: C
options.text: Begins to develop on the 4th day after fertilization

options.label: D
options.text: Is derived from the zona pellucida

options.label: E
options.text: Degenerates once cytotrophoblast takes over its function

questions.stem: Fraternal (dizygotic) twins:

options.label: E
options.text: may come from two oocytes from the same ovary

options.label: F
options.text: may come from oocytes from both ovaries

options.label: G
options.text: may be of the same sex

questions.stem: Identical (monozygotic) twins:

options.label: A
options.text: may come from two secondary oocytes

notes.H: Each has its own unless conjoined.

questions.stem: About implantation:

options.label: A
options.text: The zona pellucida breaks down after implantation

options.label: C
options.text: Attachment occurs at the embryonic pole

options.label: D
options.text: Early on, the decidua capsularis lies between conceptus and myometrium

options.label: E
options.text: Early on, the decidua basalis covers the conceptus toward the uterine cavity

options.label: F
options.text: The chorion laeve forms against the decidua capsularis

options.label: G
options.text: The chorion frondosum forms against the decidua parietalis

options.label: H
options.text: The endometrium is secretory at implantation

options.label: I
options.text: After implantation the endometrium becomes proliferative

options.label: J
options.text: The syncytiotrophoblast is in direct contact with maternal tissue

questions.stem: Which mesoderm contributes to the formation of the amniotic membrane in an embryo?
questions.why: The amnion is lined outside by extraembryonic somatic (somatopleuric) mesoderm.

notes.A: Splanchnic mesoderm covers the yolk sac.
notes.D: Intermediate mesoderm forms the urogenital ridge.

questions.stem: Which of the following forms the floor of the amniotic cavity?
questions.why: The epiblast (future ectoderm) forms the floor of the amniotic cavity.

notes.A: The amnion forms its roof and walls.
notes.B: Mesoderm lies between ecto- and endoderm.
notes.E: The hypoblast/endoderm forms the roof of the yolk sac.

questions.stem: Structures that become partly enclosed within the umbilical cord include:

notes.A: It persists in the cord until about week 10.
notes.B: The amnion covers the cord; the cavity lies outside it.
notes.C: Its stalk (vitelline duct) runs in the cord.
notes.E: The chorion is in the placenta and membranes.

questions.why: The umbilical cord encloses the connecting stalk (allantois, umbilical vessels), the yolk sac stalk and, early on, part of the extraembryonic coelom (with the herniated midgut).

questions.stem: Which of the following spaces does the enlargement of the amniotic cavity in the course of foetal development directly obliterate?
questions.why: The growing amnion fuses with the chorion and obliterates the chorionic cavity (extraembryonic coelom).

notes.A: The yolk sac shrinks but is not obliterated by the amnion.
notes.C: The blastocyst cavity is gone long before.
notes.E: The uterine cavity is obliterated by fusion of decidua capsularis and parietalis.

questions.stem: The placenta produces ALL of the following hormones EXCEPT:
questions.why: LH comes from the pituitary; the placenta makes hCG, hCS (hPL), progesterone and oestrogens.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT included in structures constituting the foetal membranes?
questions.why: Fetal membranes: amnion, chorion, yolk sac, allantois, umbilical cord and (fetal) placenta. The hypoblast is an early layer, not a membrane.

notes.E: The fetal part is a membrane.

questions.stem: Which hormone is directly responsible for maintenance of the corpus luteum of pregnancy?
questions.why: hCG from the syncytiotrophoblast keeps the corpus luteum going in early pregnancy.

questions.stem: The maternal and fetal components of the placenta are, respectively:

options.label: A
options.text: Decidua basalis and Chorion frondosum respectively

options.label: B
options.text: Decidua capsularis and Chorion leave respectively

options.label: C
options.text: Decidua parietalis and Decidua capsularis respectively

options.label: D
options.text: Chorion leave and Decidua parietalis respectively

options.label: E
options.text: Decidua basalis and Chorion leave respectively

notes.D: Fetal and maternal reversed, and not the placenta.

questions.stem: Which of the following hormones is not produced by the placenta?
What is the maternal contribution to the placenta?

notes.C: Lines the rest of the uterus.

questions.stem: Which is the foetal component of the placenta?
The chorion includes which of the following?
questions.why: The chorion is extraembryonic somatic mesoderm plus both trophoblast layers.

questions.stem: When the chorionic cavity forms that splits extraembryonic mesoderm into two layers, it extends everywhere around the embryo, EXCEPT:
questions.why: The connecting (body) stalk is where extraembryonic mesoderm stays attached.

questions.stem: Cells from which of the following grow into the blastocoele before it is converted into the chorionic cavity?
questions.why: Extraembryonic mesoderm fills the space between trophoblast and yolk sac before cavities form in it.

questions.stem: Which structure developed in the second week is responsible for changes in the third week?
questions.why: The epiblast gives all three germ layers at gastrulation.

questions.stem: The amniotic fluid that ruptures during delivery of the baby is formed by which of the following cavities?
The volume of amniotic fluid is tightly regulated, and abnormalities can occur. Which of the following is NOT a function of amniotic fluid?

options.label: A
options.text: Protection of fetus from external trauma

options.label: B
options.text: Facilitation of movement of the fetus

options.label: D
options.text: Prevention of adhesion between fetus and amnion

questions.stem: The umbilical cord contains two arteries and one vein. Which of the following forms the core supporting structure (Wharton’s jelly)?
In a late placenta, the barrier between maternal blood and fetal capillary blood includes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.why: In the late placenta the cytotrophoblast layer is largely gone.

questions.stem: The chorion includes ALL of the following EXCEPT:
questions.why: The chorion is extraembryonic somatic mesoderm with the cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast.

questions.stem: Which hormone is routinely tested for in urine to confirm a pregnancy?
Why must an obstetrician worry when a delivered placenta has missing tissue likely retained in the uterus?

options.label: A
options.text: Retained tissue may stop the myometrium contracting

options.label: C
options.text: Risk of infection as the tissue decays

options.label: D
options.text: Retained tissue may give rise to choriocarcinoma

questions.stem: At delivery of the placenta, through which layer of the decidua does separation occur?
questions.why: The placenta separates through the spongy layer of the decidua basalis.

questions.stem: About progesterone from the placenta:

options.label: A
options.text: Routine urine pregnancy tests detect it

options.label: C
options.text: It suppresses uterine contractility in pregnancy

options.label: E
options.text: It thickens the cervical mucus plug

options.label: F
options.text: It relaxes the cervix to promote labour

options.label: H
options.text: It prevents lactation until after birth

options.label: I
options.text: Its level starts to fall early in the third trimester

options.label: J
options.text: Drugs that block it can end a pregnancy

questions.stem: About human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG):

options.label: A
options.text: It is called "the hormone of pregnancy" for maintaining the endometrium

options.label: B
options.text: It is the first hormone secreted by the placenta

options.label: C
options.text: It maintains the corpus luteum of pregnancy

options.label: E
options.text: Its level rises steadily throughout pregnancy

options.label: F
options.text: It signals maternal recognition of pregnancy

options.label: G
options.text: It is linked with morning sickness

options.label: I
options.text: It is secreted by the cytotrophoblast

options.label: J
options.text: It is very high in molar pregnancy

notes.E: It peaks at about 8–10 weeks then falls.

questions.stem: Human chorionic somatomammotrophin (hCS):

options.label: A
options.text: is also called human placental lactogen

options.label: C
options.text: peaks at 8 weeks and then falls

options.label: E
options.text: reduces maternal glucose use, sparing glucose for the fetus

notes.D: It only adds to breast growth in pregnancy.

questions.stem: About placental oestrogens:

options.label: B
options.text: High late levels increase myometrial oxytocin receptors

options.label: C
options.text: They drive genital differentiation in male embryos

options.label: E
options.text: About 90% is used by the fetus

notes.A: They work with it for most of pregnancy.

questions.stem: The notochord develops from which of the following structures?
questions.why: The primitive node (Hensen's knot) gives rise to the notochordal process.

notes.A: It lines the chorion and forms the connecting stalk.
notes.B: It produces intraembryonic mesoderm, not the notochord.
notes.D: The endoderm only briefly takes in the notochordal plate.
notes.E: It forms from ectoderm above the notochord.

questions.stem: Which is the part in the caudal region of the embryo where ectoderm and endoderm remain in direct contact during the formation of the trilaminar disc?
questions.why: At the cloacal membrane (and the oropharyngeal membrane at the head end) ectoderm and endoderm stay fused with no mesoderm between.

notes.A: This is at the cranial end.
notes.B: The node is where cells invaginate.
notes.C: Mesoderm streams out from the streak.
notes.D: It lies cranially, in front of the notochord.

questions.stem: Which structure in the trilaminar embryonic disc induces the formation of the neural plate?
questions.why: The notochord induces the overlying ectoderm to thicken into the neural plate.

notes.C: It lines the chorion and yolk sac.
notes.D: It forms somites, etc.; induction comes from the notochord.

questions.stem: Which of the following mesodermal layers gives rise to somites in the embryo?

notes.A: Forms body wall and gut wall mesoderm.

questions.stem: The mesoderm that gives rise to the somites is:
The last layer of the trilaminar embryonic disc to develop is:
questions.why: Intraembryonic mesoderm forms during gastrulation (week 3), after epiblast and hypoblast.

questions.stem: A sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT) is a tumour that may be found in the newborn, situated in the midline just anterior to the vertebral column. Which of the following is thought to give rise to SCT?
questions.why: Remnants of the primitive streak can give a sacrococcygeal teratoma.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures establishes axial symmetry in the embryo?
questions.why: The notochord defines the midline axis.

questions.stem: Cells from which of the following gives rise to the primitive streak?
questions.why: The primitive streak forms from epiblast (future ectoderm) cells.

questions.stem: During the 4th week of development, the head fold of the embryo is described. Which of the following mechanisms is responsible for brain formation?
Which of the following layers in the trilaminar embryonic disc contributes to development of the urinary system?
The body cavities are potential spaces that become real as development proceeds around some endodermal viscera. What is the primordial coelomic cavity?
In which part of the embryo does the coelom of the body cavities develop?
questions.why: Spaces in the lateral plate split it into somatic and splanchnic layers around the coelom.

questions.stem: During folding in the head region, a thick mass of mesoderm (septum transversum) separates structures but leaves openings on each side. What are these openings called?
Which of the multiple structures that form the diaphragm becomes the central tendon?
Which of the following is NOT a derivative of the endodermal foregut?
questions.why: The spleen is mesodermal (dorsal mesogastrium).
